story: Halong, one year on. The forecasts are now AI and the observations under them have holes (runner-up, NOAA's inventory of AI in Alaska fish science on crab opener week)

KTOO republished it word for word on October 15th (https://www.ktoo.org/2026/10/15/halong-1-year-after-the-storm/); that is the same reporting, not independent corroboration. KYUK editor's note dated October 16th, 2026.

claims.claim: KYUK identifies Rick Thoman as a climatologist.

claims.claim: Thoman said ex-typhoon Halong was uniquely challenging for forecasters.

claims.notes: Reporter's paraphrase of Thoman.

claims.claim: Thoman said global models did a good job forecasting Halong's track into the Bering Sea.
claims.verbatim: He said that global models did a good job forecasting its track into the Bering Sea, but failed to forecast the storm's eastward shift.
claims.notes: 'He' is Thoman. This sentence directly follows 'Climatologist Thoman said that ex-typhoon Halong was uniquely challenging for forecasters.' Reporter's paraphrase. 'Global models' are not identified as AI models. Never say an AI model forecast Halong (AIGFS went operational in December 2025, after the storm).

claims.claim: Thoman said global models failed to forecast Halong's eastward shift.
claims.verbatim: He said that global models did a good job forecasting its track into the Bering Sea, but failed to forecast the storm's eastward shift.

claims.claim: KYUK reported that a lack of weather balloon launches at sites across Western Alaska may have played a role.
claims.verbatim: A lack of weather balloon launches at sites across Western Alaska may have played a role.

claims.notes: Reporter's narration, not a Thoman quote. The sentence doesn't say what the role was in. By page order it directly follows the 'failed to forecast the storm's eastward shift' sentence, so the forecast miss is the contextual referent. Keep 'may have'. Never connect balloons or station outages to deaths or damage. KYUK doesn't name Kotzebue (see C49), and no fetched page states Kotzebue's 2026 status.

claims.claim: Thoman told KYUK that ocean observations are needed.
claims.verbatim: We need ocean observations.
claims.notes: Direct quote from Rick Thoman. The next sentence on the page is C08.

claims.claim: Thoman told KYUK that current observations are needed especially where local effects matter.
claims.verbatim: We need current observations, especially where these local effects matter so much.
claims.notes: Direct Thoman quote. Note that it contains the house-banned word 'matter' only as 'matter so much' (word_ban bans 'matters', and 'matter' as a whole word may be flagged). A straight-quoted verbatim passage keeps its words under the house rule, but copy should confirm with word_ban.py before using it on a slide.

claims.claim: Thoman said the observations he wants go beyond more Federal Aviation Administration weather stations.

claims.notes: Direct Thoman quote. The bracketed text is KYUK's insertion; keep the brackets if quoted.

claims.notes: Direct Rick Thoman quote. 'Three' means ex-typhoons, from the surrounding context (C16).

claims.notes: Reporter's paraphrase of Braun. Braun is also quoted as saying 'With every single storm, we're doing better', per the summary (not separately confirmed verbatim).

claims.claim: Ex-Typhoon Halong caused widespread inundation along the Kuskokwim Delta coast on October 12th, 2025.

claims.claim: FEMA's disaster declaration DR-4893-AK covers severe storms, flooding and the remnants of Typhoon Halong over an incident period of October 8th to 13th, 2025.
claims.notes: PRIMARY. Background (before the window). Page title: Alaska Severe Storms, Flooding, and Remnants of Typhoon Halong (DR-4893-AK). The verbatim contains a hyphen as printed on the page. date_of_source is the page's 'Last updated' date.
